previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with symptoms of urinary tract infection following a nephrostomy tube and stent replacement, including low-grade fever, chills, nausea, and flank pain. She was started on linezolid for presumed infection, and urine cultures later confirmed E. coli, leading to a switch to oral cefpodoxime. Leakage around the tube persisted, prompting a second tube replacement, after which drainage improved and symptoms resolved. Her kidney function stabilized with creatinine returning to baseline. A psychiatry consult addressed her emotional distress related to recurrent hospitalizations and family stress, and she was transitioned from atovaquone to dapsone due to nausea. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor nephrostomy output, continue antibiotics, and follow up with the transplant and mental health teams.

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment/Plan: ___ F s/p ECD kidney transplant ___ for PKD

___ with fever, hematuria, and dysuria concerning for UTI

# UTI: pt had large leuk esterase on U/A on admission suspicious 
for UTI, so nephrostomy tube was uncapped. She had a history of 
enterococcal UTI so she was treated empirically with linezolid 
and ceftriaxone.  She felt generally unwell upon admission and 
spiked a fever on hospital day 2, but she gradually improved 
over the next few days and subsequently remained afebrile.  A 
renal u/s was done which showed a normal transplanted kidney and 
no fluid collections, with variable diastolic flow in the upper 
pole. Urine culture grew out pan-sensitive Klebsiella, so she 
was transitioned from ceftriaxone to cefpoxodime and linezolid 
was stopped.  She will finish a 14d course of cefpodoxime as an 
outpatient with plans to perform repeat urine culture to ensure 
resolution of infection.

# afib: pt was continued on rate control with metoprolol and 
also on amiodarone, however, metoprolol dose was decreased to 
50mg po BID.  INR was supratherapeutic to 3.4 on discharge so 
coumadin dose was decreased to 2.5mg po daily with plans to 
recheck INR a few days after discharge.

# renal transplant: myfortic dose was decreased to 360mg po BID. 
 Tacrolimus was continued at home dose.  Pt had been scheduled 
for nephrostogram and possible ureteral stricure dilatation 
prior to admission, but this was postponed because of patient's 
infection.  She was instructed to keep her nephro tube uncapped.

# HTN: pt's creatinine elevated to 2.5 on admission so lasix was 
held.  Creatinine improved to 2.0 by discharge so lasix was 
restarted and decreased to once and day from original dosing of 
twice a day.
  
# ___ murmur:  pt has h/o systolic murmur but physical exam 
findings were suggestive of new diastolic component.  Given pt's 
recent history of syncope, an echo was obtained to evaluate the 
new murmur.  It showed an increased physiologic pulmonic valve 
regurgitation and worsened pulmonary hypertension, but no other 
new findings.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with history of renal transplant in ___
complicated by delayed graft function and recurrent UTIs.  Patient also with
ureteral stricture requiring percutaneous nephrostomy tube.  Evaluation for
perinephric abscess.

COMPARISON:  Renal ultrasounds from ___.

RENAL ULTRASOUND:  The transplanted kidney in the right lower quadrant
measures 11.7 cm.  A percutaneous nephrostomy drain is identified within the
collecting system.  No perinephric hematoma or fluid collection is identified
to suggest abscess.  Doppler evaluation of the mid and lower pole segmental
renal arteries demonstrate sharp arterial upstroke and diastolic flow
throughout, with resistive indices measuring 0.73.  Arterial waveforms of the
upper pole renal artery demonstrate a sharp upstroke and measured RI is normal
but in some of the cardiac cyscle the diastolic flow is closer to the
baseline.  Recommend close interval follow-up ultrasound.  

IMPRESSION:
1.  Normal grayscale images of the transplanted kidney without surrounding
fluid collection.
2.  Nephrostomy catheter within the collecting system.
3.  Variable diastolic flow in the upper pole of the transplanted kidney. 
Recommend close interval followup with repeat renal Doppler ultrasound.
